quarterly_data.signal: Margin and 2027 outlook (CFO Dado Alonso): 'Even as we continue to invest in growth, we see a clear path to capturing more margin, not just this year, but in 2027 and well beyond. We have visibility into pricing and expect capacity coming online from our own data center to begin improving margins in the second half of next year.' He expects capacity deployed late in Q2 to begin contributing to revenue in Q3. The deals closed in Q2, which start coming online from late Q4, 'can serve as the baseline for pricing early next year'; Nebius will deploy 'significantly more capacity in 2027' than in 2026, and expects the asset-light model, along with high-value services such as agentic and inference solutions, to contribute an increasing share of revenue while supporting even higher margins. Formal 2027 guidance will be provided later this year.
quarterly_data.figure: margins from own data-center capacity to begin improving in the second half of next year; formal 2027 guidance later this year

quarterly_data.signal: Pipeline and landmark-deal detail (Marc Boroditsky): 'Yes, we have more deals just like them.' Q2 pipeline generation stepped up again and 'includes multiple opportunities over $1 billion, spanning AI natives, Neolabs, and enterprises.' One of the four landmark customers was introduced to Nebius by a key strategic partner late in Q1, was looking for a large-scale contiguous GB300 cluster with flexibility for future expansion, and closed in May, citing Nebius' ability to serve its current U.S. deployment needs as well as future sovereign expansion; Nebius is now in discussions with it for more capacity and it is exploring Token Factory. All four wins came after multiple engagement cycles and hands-on proofs of concept, and Nebius is in discussions with several of the four on post-training and inference.

Capacity allocation priorities (Marc Boroditsky, on splitting 2027 capacity between short-dated and multi-year deals): Nebius optimizes 'across customer type, price, payment structure, duration, and deal size' rather than a single metric such as ACV per megawatt. 'Our current emphasis is taking care of existing customers, followed by new logos, and then terms. Terms in order of priority, including price, then upfront prepayment, then duration.' Capacity deployed in the latter half of 2026 and into 2027 will be allocated across both medium- and short-term deals.

CEO Arkady Volozh on the market: 'The whole AI cloud market is growing massively from hundreds of billions of dollars per year to probably trillions.' Prices 'are changing fast, they're growing'; Nebius' model was built 'to build capacity in advance, but not to pre-sell it in advance', which leaves available capacity to allocate to shorter-term and much higher-margin contracts. The first auction (for a midterm contract) was possible because Nebius had free unallocated capacity and a multi-tenant platform, and because the platform 'is universal and able to work on any third-party capacity' Nebius can grow faster through the asset-light model.
quarterly_data.figure: AI cloud market growing from hundreds of billions of dollars per year to probably trillions

quarterly_data.signal: Delivery flexibility (Andrey Korolenko): 'the vast majority of our contracts is the cloud contracts, where we have the flexibility where, within the region, we can deliver it, reducing the dependency on any one location.' Over-provisioning capacity is 'our highest priority for today'; the general approach is to deploy as much capacity as Nebius can and to build in advance as much as it can.

Token Factory and Tavily (Roman Chernin): the 'Agent AI and Clarify teams' (as transcribed) are 'fully integrated into the Token Factory effort and already shipping inside our roadmap'; independent benchmarks continue to rank Nebius among the leading inference platforms; Nebius' own infrastructure agent, shipped at the last cloud release, runs an open-source model served by Token Factory; Tavily achieved a set of certifications for enterprise deployments. Nebius positions Token Factory for reliable high-performance inference and post-training, and Tavily for grounding as companies move from closed ecosystems with built-in search toward more open ecosystems.
